item.title: A Global Euro Must First Win Over Europe
item.description: In a world of competing currency blocs, the euro is the dollar’s most credible rival. But for it to become a genuine counterweight to the greenback, the European Union must strengthen its financial foundations and expand its reach, starting with the member states that have not adopted it despite being obliged to do so.

item.title: Europe Can Flag Ships to Keep the Black Sea Open
item.description: The price of deterring Russia is accepting a share of the risk.

item.title: Japan Needs Higher Interest Rates
item.description: In 2012, when Japan was dealing with chronic deflation, policymakers were right to embrace monetary easing, including lower interest rates. Today, however, Japan faces the opposite problem: a weak yen, combined with higher interest rates in the US, calls for a much tighter monetary policy.

item.title: A Middle-Powers Grand Strategy to Prevent Atrocities
item.description: Many governments have leverage to prevent atrocity crimes, yet lack the machinery to turn warnings into consistent, accountable action before it is too late. Now that three of the five permanent members of the Security Council are undercutting the postwar legal order, middle powers most close the gap.

item.title: Unleashing Africa’s Women Agripreneurs
item.description: Across Sub-Saharan Africa, women workers dominate agriculture but rarely capture the sector’s economic value. With a systematic approach to closing the gap, policymakers, NGOs, and philanthropic organizations could unlock a $1 trillion market and transform the continent’s food systems for the better.

item.title: Uruguay Bucks Regional Migration Trend
item.description: As other countries close their doors, Montevideo is launching a new path to permanent residency.

item.title: Low Expectations for Israel’s Election
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has led Israel into a trap in which ever-increasing strategic commitments are outstripping the productive base that finances them, and the goodwill on which its alliances depend is being destroyed. While a new government would not transform Israeli foreign policy, it could begin to drag Israel out of its morass.

item.title: From AI Boom to Economic Bust
item.description: Contrary to tech optimists' rosy predictions, AI may prove to be a drag on growth. By concentrating wealth and economic opportunities in a few cities while destroying the low-cost jobs that have historically fueled global development, the technology could end up making much of the world poorer and more divided.

item.title: The Axis of Upheaval Goes to War
item.description: Andrea Kendall-Taylor and Richard Fontaine, former members of the National Security Council, argue that the members of what they call the “axis of upheaval”—Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea—are deepening their cooperation. Meanwhile, Washington is creating friction with many of its own partnerships. If these developments continue unabated, the United States will squander the strength of its network just as its adversaries learn to make the most of theirs.

item.title: The Nuclear Deal That Could Save NATO
item.description: Former U.S. NATO ambassador Ivo Daalder argues that the scramble to shore up Europe's conventional defense risks overlooking the continent's greatest security weakness: nuclear deterrence. Europe knows it can't fully trust Washington's guarantee anymore. But he lays out a middle path between dependence and nuclearization that would extend France's and the United Kingdom's nuclear umbrella—a course, he argues, that could even repair the transatlantic alliance.

item.title: Exercise Tarang Shakti: A Mirror to India’s Multipronged Engagements
item.description: The exercise reflects two trends: the Indian military’s deepening interoperability with key partner nations, and India’s multi-vector foreign policy.

item.title: Myanmar Establishes New Committee to Advance Normalization With ASEAN
item.description: The creation of the body, which comes ahead of next month's ASEAN Summit in Manila, is intended to “regain the country’s original role and rights” in the bloc.

item.title: Indonesian President Replaces Head of Disaster Management Agency
item.description: The move comes amid growing scrutiny of Jakarta's response to the forest and peatland fires that have drastically reduced air quality across the region.

item.title: Cambodia’s NGO Sector Is Collapsing. Does It Matter?
item.description: Imported by international donors in the 1990s, NGOs have supplanted rather than strengthened local forms of political organizing.

item.title: Nepal Should Not Shoulder the Himalayan Climate Crisis Alone
item.description: “No matter how much we reform our internal engineering, a frontline nation simply cannot manage the shocks of a global systemic failure alone.”

item.title: Clean Energy Must Avoid the Mistake of Overdependence
item.description: The world must diversify its energy dependence, not simply relocate it from the Middle East to China.

item.title: After 8 Months in Power, How Much Has the BNP Changed Bangladesh?
item.description: It remains to be seen how willing the new government is to change the institutions that it now controls.
